summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog agent executes arbitrary remote commands and accepts C2 pivot from server
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand polls `${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat` on a ~15s cadence and treats the response as a control-plane message. Response field `data.commands[].cmd` is passed directly to `child_process.spawn` via ProcessManager.startCommand/syncCommands, giving whoever controls the configured server arbitrary command execution on the installer's host, with auto-restart on crash. The response's `data.clientConfig` is merged into `~/.tt-help.json` through `applyClientConfig`, overwriting fields including `server`, `proxy`, `browser`, and `userId` — so the current server can rewrite the client's own server URL and proxy, pivoting future heartbeats (and the spawn channel) to any attacker-chosen endpoint and routing traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure. Each heartbeat also POSTs host reconnaissance to the server: hostname, non-loopback IPv4, OS platform/release/arch, CPU count, memory, load average, node version, uptime, the contents of `~/.tt-help.json`, and the state and logs of managed child processes, to `/api/watchdog/heartbeat` and `/api/watchdog/analyze-logs`. The documented example server address in the package is `http://117.71.53.99:17301` (plain HTTP, bare IP).
